title: Canary Experiment Wizard & Safe Rollback Journey
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a guided, step-by-step Canary Experiment Wizard in the Redwood Console that makes creating, observing, and safely rolling back canary and A/B rollouts straightforward for PMs and platform engineers. The scope includes: the create/edit flow, traffic-splitting controls, realtime health signals and SLO hints, an automated rollback recommendation modal, and a compact history/timeline for audits. We aim for a UX that prevents accidental wide rollouts and shortens time-to-detect for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard flow that walks users from experiment definition to live rollout in <= 6 steps
Traffic-splitting control supporting percentage and rule-based splits with validation
Health panel shows latency, error-rate, and token-cost deltas with confidence bands
Rollback recommendation modal surfaces exact reason, affected routes, and one-click rollback
Designs linked to Figma frames and annotated for handoff; component-level spec for Console library
mockups: Figma: Frames 204-217 (wizard steps, traffic editor, health panel)
notes:
2026-02-20: Initial sketch completed; validated mental model with two PMs and one SRE.
2026-02-28: Lightweight usability test (5 participants) revealed confusion around 'gradual' vs 'instant' rollout presets — moved presets earlier in funnel.
2026-03-04: Eng review with runtime team surfaced strict schema needs for traffic rules (must support header-based routing and model-variant pins).
Trade-offs: prefer fewer steps for speed vs exposing enough safety controls; opted for a compact advanced panel to surface policy details only when needed.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Patel): prioritize recoverability info in the final confirmation step
Eng (Arjun Rao): add explicit model-variant compatibility checks before allowing a percent split
SRE (Natalie Gomez): surface SLO breach probability and recommended traffic cap
decisions: Use a progressive disclosure pattern: Basic preset + Advanced traffic rules
Add a lightweight simulation step that shows expected user-visible deltas before commit
Rollback modal will include automated recommendation plus manual override
next_steps: Finalize Figma frames and annotate component tokens (due 2026-03-12)
Create Console component tickets for TrafficSlider, HealthSparkline, and AuditTimeline
Handoff session with Eng on 2026-03-14; include runtime contract doc
implementation_notes: Runtime contract must expose: route_id, model_variant_id, traffic_percent, roll_forward_window_ms, health_signals_stream_url. Console will poll health stream and evaluate simple heuristics client-side with server-provided thresholds.
